section_1.title: Introduction: The Image Synthesis Pipeline
section_1.content: A 30-second overview of how text prompts transform into high-resolution images. Introduce the two pillars: CLIP (the 'Understanding' bridge) and Diffusion (the 'Creation' engine).
section_1.example: Visualizing a text prompt 'A robot painting a sunset' turning into a pixelated sketch, then a refined image.

section_2.title: CLIP: Mapping Language to Visual Space
section_2.content: Explain Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP). Concept: Mapping text and image embeddings into a shared high-dimensional vector space using cosine similarity. Prerequisite: Dot products measure alignment.
section_2.example: A graph showing an image vector and a text vector pointing in the same direction in 3D space, showing their 'alignment' score.

section_3.title: The Diffusion Process: Math as an Artist
section_3.content: Introduce Forward Diffusion (adding Gaussian noise) and Reverse Diffusion (denoising). Math concept: Markov Chains. We learn a neural network to predict the noise component ε at each step t.
section_3.example: An animation of a clear photo of a 'Golden Retriever' gradually turning into static white noise, then reversing the process.

section_4.title: Guidance: Bridging Text and Noise
section_4.content: Explain how the CLIP embedding influences the denoising step. We use 'Classifier-Free Guidance' to push the diffusion model to predict noise that aligns better with the text prompt vector.
section_4.example: A vector field showing the noise-prediction gradient being 'tilted' or steered by the text input toward the desired image content.

section_5.title: Synthesis and Conclusion
section_5.content: Summarize the iterative refinement process. The model starts with pure noise and performs 50-100 denoising steps, each steered by CLIP, to arrive at a coherent image.
section_5.example: A summary graphic: [Prompt] -> [CLIP Embedding] -> [Denoising Loop] -> [High-Res Image of a Cyberpunk City].

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
